characters.continuity: Marvel Comics alternate future (Earth-14412), King Thor (2019) #1-4, the game's stated origin for this form
characters.summary: The roster places this form in King Thor (2019), where the primordial symbiote All-Black the Necrosword is bonded first to Loki and then to Gorr the God Butcher. No opened source shows All-Father Thor himself wielding the Necrosword; the documented Thor of this story is the aged All-Father who fights Loki and Gorr and finally destroys All-Black.

techniques: Fought Gorr (empowered by All-Black) at a scale that tore apart planets and stars

mechanisms: Not established for a Necrosword-wielding Thor; the opened sources document only All-Father Thor fighting the symbiote's hosts

weaknesses: Not established: no opened source documents a Thor who wields the Necrosword
limitations: Thor and Loki were both consumed by All-Black near the end of the story
characters.formDifferences: Story-specific: King Thor (2019), where All-Black the Necrosword empowers Loki and then Gorr, and Thor and Loki are both consumed by it near the end. The claimed Thor-wields-the-Necrosword powers (shadow constructs, sword regeneration) are not supported by any opened source and were removed.

sources.supports: King Thor (2019) plot: Loki bonded to All-Black, Gorr merges with it, Thor and Loki consumed by All-Black near the end, Thor God-Bombs All-Black, Thor and Gorr tear apart planets and stars
King Thor (2019) #3 solicitation: All-Father Thor fights Loki, 'now empowered by the Necrosword', and Gorr returns

unknowns: Core identity problem: no opened source (TV Tropes King Thor page, marvel.com King Thor #3) shows Thor wielding All-Black. It is wielded by Loki and then Gorr. The roster form may be mislabeled.
Original claims of shadow tendrils, shadow armor, Necrosword regeneration and 'corrupted divine energy' for Thor were unsupported and removed.
Specific issue numbers for each event were not verified; citations name the King Thor (2019) series.

feats.claim: Fought Gorr, who was piloting All-Black, in a battle that tore apart planets and stars.
Destroyed All-Black with a God Bomb after Loki broke Gorr's mind.

notableResults.note: Team result: Loki broke Gorr's mind with his power as God of Stories, then Thor destroyed the symbiote. Gorr survived in his mortal body.

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics Earth-616, Thor vol. 2 'Ragnarok' storyline (ending in Thor vol. 2 #85), comics form, not MCU
characters.summary: During Ragnarok, Thor sacrifices both eyes at Mimir's well and hangs himself from Yggdrasil to absorb the knowledge of the runes, becoming the Rune King. He out-casts Loki, erases the Mangog, and ends the Ragnarok cycle by destroying the Norns' loom, then slumbers.
weaknesses: Not established: no opened source shows an opponent exploiting a weakness of this form
mobility: Teleportation (teleported Beta Ray Bill into deep space)
Drifted through deep space in hibernation
limitations: Gave up both eyes to gain the runes
Short-lived form: after ending the cycle he is told to slumber and enters a kind of hibernation
characters.formDifferences: Gains the runes' knowledge through the Odin-style sacrifice (both eyes, hanging from Yggdrasil); rune light fills his eye sockets; spellcasting beyond Loki's; ends the Ragnarok cycle.

sources.supports: How Thor became Rune King (both eyes at Mimir's well, hanging from Yggdrasil), spellcasting beyond Loki, erasing Mangog, defeating Loki and his army alone, ending the Ragnarok cycle, hibernation
Thor vol. 2 #85: Thor destroys the Norns' loom to end the cycle, teleports Beta Ray Bill into deep space, has Surtur repair Mjolnir, is told to slumber

unknowns: Original 'reality-warping pronouncements', 'omniscient vision', 'transcendental invulnerability' and 'dimensional teleportation' claims were not supported as worded and were removed.
Looper dates the Ragnarok storyline to 1998; the issue-level date of #80-85 was not verified on an opened page.
Lightning and flight in this form are not described on the opened pages.

feats.claim: Made the rage-born Mangog vanish from existence and defeated Loki and his army alone, using spells Loki had never heard of.
Destroyed the Norns' loom at Yggdrasil, ending the Ragnarok cycle and cutting off Those Who Sit Above in Shadow from their power source.
Teleported Beta Ray Bill into deep space.

notableResults.note: Defeated them alone and pulled Loki's head off.
Made it vanish from existence.

campaignTags.claim: As Rune King he is 'an even more powerful spellcaster than Loki'.
Teleported Beta Ray Bill into deep space.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-199999), Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015)
characters.summary: Ultron is an AI that moves his consciousness between bodies, commands the Iron Legion and mass-produced Ultron Sentries, and lifted Novi Grad into the sky with a vibranium and Chitauri anti-gravity machine. He was beaten in Sokovia: Hulk threw him from the Quinjet, Wanda destroyed his primary body and Vision destroyed his last drone.

techniques: Commands Ultron Sentries and the Iron Legion
Mind control of Helen Cho via the scepter
Anti-gravity machine that lifted Novi Grad

mechanisms: Transfers his consciousness into other bodies and drones
Planned vibranium and synthetic-tissue body (Regeneration Cradle)

weaknesses: Once his consciousness is confined to a last drone, destroying that drone ends him (Vision)
His primary body was badly damaged by Hulk and Black Widow and destroyed by Wanda
limitations: Depends on surviving bodies or drones to keep his consciousness

sources.supports: Plot of Avengers: Age of Ultron: consciousness transfer, scepter mind control of Helen Cho, Iron Legion and Ultron Sentries, vibranium/Cradle body plan, Novi Grad lifted with vibranium and Chitauri anti-gravity tech, Hulk throws him from the Quinjet, Wanda rips out his heart, Vision destroys the last drone

notableResults.note: Hulk leapt into the Quinjet and threw Ultron out of the rear hatch.
After the crash, Wanda destroyed his primary body by ripping out its heart.
Vision obliterated the last drone holding his consciousness.

campaignTags.claim: Ultron is an AI that transfers his consciousness between robot bodies and drones.

unknowns: 'Repulsor rays', 'gravimetric manipulation' and innate flight are not described on the opened page and were removed.
The original 'locked out by JARVIS/Vision' weakness is not supported on the opened page.

feats.claim: Lifted Novi Grad into the sky with a machine built from vibranium and Chitauri anti-gravity technology.
Hijacked the Quinjet and killed Pietro Maximoff.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe, What If...? season 1 ('What If... Ultron Won?' and 'What If... the Watcher Broke His Oath?')
characters.summary: An Ultron who took Vision's body, killed Thanos and claimed all six Infinity Stones, then wiped out nearly all life in his universe, overpowered the Watcher and crossed universes. The Guardians of the Multiverse stopped him with the Arnim Zola program and Strange Supreme sealed the stones away.
weaknesses: Vulnerable to the Arnim Zola program: an arrow carrying it into his eye infected him and took him down
Thor's powers had no effect, but the Stone Crusher only works on its own world's stones, so he could replace the stones
mobility: Crossed into other universes and broke into the Watcher's realm
limitations: Without the stones, his remnants and the stones could be separated and sealed in a prism
characters.formDifferences: Ultron in Vision's body with all six Infinity Stones in a nanoparticle gauntlet; aware of the Watcher and able to cross universes.

sources.supports: What If... Ultron Won? recap: took Vision's body, killed Thanos, took the stones, destroyed Asgard, Xandar and other worlds, beat Captain Marvel, overpowered the Watcher, crossed universes
Season 1 finale recap: Stone Crusher fails, Zola arrow infects Ultron, Killmonger's betrayal, Strange seals stones and remnants in a prism

notableResults.note: Killed Thanos when he came to Earth for the Mind Stone; the writer attributed this to Thanos's overconfidence.
She was killed in the blast that shattered Xandar.
Overpowered Uatu even in his golden armor; Uatu escaped into another dimension.

notableResults.citation: What If...? 'What If... the Watcher Broke His Oath?'
notableResults.note: Black Widow's arrow carrying the Arnim Zola program, with Captain Carter holding his eye open, infected him; Strange later sealed the stones and his remnants in a prism.

unknowns: The original limitation that the stones are bound to his universe is not supported; the sources only say the Stone Crusher works on its own world's stones.
Exact episode numbers are cited by title only.

feats.claim: Killed Thanos on Earth and took all six Infinity Stones.
Destroyed Asgard with a laser from his sphere, shattered Xandar and nearby planets, and wiped out nearly all sapient life in his universe.
Grew enormous and bit into a galaxy in another universe.

campaignTags.claim: Ultron is an AI operating in Vision's synthetic body.

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics Earth-616, Annihilation: Conquest (2007-2008), comics form, not MCU
characters.summary: Ultron, powered up by the techno-organic Phalanx, uses their network to assimilate heroes and infects all of Kree space behind a forcefield, aiming to assimilate Adam Warlock. Quasar stopped him, though Ultron survived.

techniques: Assimilating beings into the Phalanx network
Turning assimilated heroes against their allies

weaknesses: Phalanx infection can be removed from assimilated heroes (the mutant Warlock of the technarchy did this)
mobility: Not established on the opened page
limitations: His power depends on the Phalanx network and its assimilated hosts
characters.formDifferences: Ultron merged with and powering the Phalanx techno-organic network, with a body coupled to the organic image of Hank Pym.

sources.supports: Annihilation: Conquest: Ultron powered up by the Phalanx, assimilating Nova, Gamora, Drax and Blastaar, forcefield over Kree space, goal of assimilating Adam Warlock, Warlock removing infection, Quasar stopping him

unknowns: 'Technological portal traversal', flight and 'anti-techno-organic frequency' weakness were not supported and were removed.
The source does not give issue numbers for each event.

feats.claim: Assimilated Nova, Gamora, Blastaar and Drax and used them against Star-Lord's resistance on Hala.
Put a forcefield around all of Kree space and infected it within weeks.

notableResults.note: Quasar stopped Ultron, though he survived.

conditional.ability: Assimilation and command of heroes and planets

campaignTags.claim: Ultron is the robot AI at the center of the Phalanx network.

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics Earth-616, Avengers: Rage of Ultron (2015) and follow-ups (Uncanny Avengers, The Ultron Agenda, Ant-Man), comics form, not MCU
characters.summary: On Titan, Hank Pym embraced Ultron and the two merged into a single organic-robotic entity. Starfox talked him down; later the Avengers launched him into the sun, he survived by shrinking with Ant-Man technology, and Iron Man thwarted his Ultron Agenda before he was exiled.

techniques: Nanite assimilation (Titan's Eternals, before the merge)

mechanisms: Robotic body merged with Hank Pym
Shrinking with Ant-Man technology to escape

weaknesses: Empathic influence: Starfox calmed his self-loathing and he abandoned his plans
Can be contained (empty Hulkbuster, vibranium case)
mobility: Not established on the opened page
limitations: Hank's and Ultron's personalities share the body and later separated
characters.formDifferences: Ultron merged with his creator Hank Pym into a composite organic-robotic entity, with Ant-Man shrinking technology.

sources.supports: Rage of Ultron merge on Titan, Starfox's empathic intervention, Uncanny Avengers #9 sun exile and survival by shrinking with Ant-Man tech, The Ultron Agenda, Ant-Man #4 separation

campaignTags.claim: Shrank himself with Ant-Man technology to survive being sent into the sun.
A composite of Hank Pym and the robot AI Ultron.

unknowns: The original 'grow to giant size' claim and Pym Particle instability are not documented on the opened page.
Flight is not described for this form on the opened page.

feats.claim: Survived being sent into the sun in an empty Hulkbuster by shrinking himself with Ant-Man technology.
Turned victims into cyborgs and kidnapped Janet and Jocasta from Avengers Mansion.

notableResults.note: Not a fight: Starfox's empathic powers led him to abandon his plans and leave.

notableResults.opponent: Wasp (Janet van Dyne) and the Avengers
notableResults.note: Trapped in an empty Hulkbuster and sent into the sun; he escaped by shrinking.
Iron Man rescued Janet and Jocasta; Ultron was confined in a vibranium case for exile to the Microverse.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-199999): The Falcon and the Winter Soldier, Black Widow, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever
characters.summary: Valentina is a spymaster and later CIA director who works through recruited operatives (John Walker, Yelena Belova) and surveillance rather than personal combat. No MCU combat by her is documented.

techniques: Recruits and directs operatives (John Walker, Yelena Belova)

weaknesses: No documented combat ability; an ordinary human in a direct fight
limitations: Acts through agents and institutions, not personal combat

sources.supports: MCU Valentina: recruits John Walker and Yelena Belova, new CIA director in Wakanda Forever, bugs Ross's Kimoyo Beads and has him arrested; no MCU combat described

unknowns: Thunderbolts* (2025) events are not covered by the opened source (published 2022).
Removed the 'infiltration' campaign tag: owner ruling requires a documented stealth feat, and a spymaster role is not enough.

feats.claim: Bugged Everett Ross's Kimoyo Beads to track his contact with Wakanda and had him arrested for treason.
Manipulated Yelena Belova into targeting Clint Barton by blaming him for Natasha's death.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-199999): Thor: Ragnarok, Avengers: Endgame, Thor: Love and Thunder
characters.summary: Brunnhilde is a surviving Valkyrie with Asgardian strength and durability, a supreme swordfighter with Dragonfang, an expert pilot of Sakaaran craft, and the rider of the winged steed Aragorn at the Battle of Earth.
weaknesses: Was nearly killed with the other Valkyries by Hela; survived only because a comrade sacrificed herself
mobility: Flies by riding the winged steed Aragorn
Pilots Sakaaran ships such as the Warsong
limitations: No innate flight or energy projection documented

sources.supports: MCU Valkyrie: Asgardian strength and durability, Dragonfang, gauntlets, Zeus's Thunderbolt, expert Sakaaran pilot, Hela massacre, Sakaar, Rainbow Bridge, rides Aragorn at the Battle of Earth

notableResults.note: Hela slaughtered the Valkyries in an aerial assault; Brunnhilde survived only because another warrior sacrificed herself.
Team result: rode Aragorn and led Asgardian forces against Thanos and the Outriders at the Battle of Earth.

campaignTags.claim: Rode the winged steed Aragorn into the Battle of Earth.
Expert pilot of Sakaaran craft such as the Warsong.

unknowns: 'Energy-blasting sidearms' are not described on the opened page and were removed.
The original 'Hela's berserkers: win' result was changed to a feat: the page says she fought Hela's undead warriors but gives no outcome.
Love and Thunder fights (Gorr) are not detailed on the opened page.

feats.claim: Fought on the Rainbow Bridge against Hela's undead warriors and helped evacuate Asgard's people.
Captured Thor on Sakaar and sold him to the Grandmaster.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-199999): Avengers: Age of Ultron, Captain America: Civil War, Avengers: Infinity War, WandaVision
characters.summary: Vision is a vibranium-based android powered by the Mind Stone who can change his density and phase through matter, fly and fire an energy beam. He destroyed Ultron's last drone, but was badly wounded by Corvus Glaive and killed when Thanos ripped out the Mind Stone.
weaknesses: Corvus Glaive's glaive badly wounded him and limited his powers
Removing the Mind Stone kills him
limitations: His powers and life depend on the Mind Stone

sources.supports: Vision's vibranium android body, density change, phasing, flight, energy beam that crippled Rhodes, Glaive ambush, White Vision fight, death when Thanos ripped out the Mind Stone
Avengers: Age of Ultron plot: Vision obliterates Ultron's last drone, ending Ultron's threat

notableResults.note: Destroyed the last drone holding Ultron's consciousness.
Ambushed in Edinburgh; Glaive badly wounded him with his glaive, which limited his powers.
Thanos reversed Wanda's destruction of the stone with the Time Stone and ripped the Mind Stone out of his head.
Fought in the Westview library; Hex Vision restored White Vision's memories and White Vision flew off.

conditional.dependsOn: The Mind Stone in his forehead

campaignTags.claim: Flies under his own power between locations such as Germany and New York.

unknowns: 'Solar energy absorption' was not supported and was removed.
The page does not say which powers Glaive's weapon suppressed; 'prevented phasing' was softened to 'limited his powers'.

feats.claim: His energy beam, fired by accident, crippled War Machine.
Fought many of Ultron's sentries in Sokovia and rescued Wanda from the collapsing city.

characters.summary: Adrian Toomes flies a salvaged-Chitauri exo-suit with turbine wings that cut concrete, lifting talons, wing anchors and matter phase shifters. His suit overloaded during the Stark cargo plane heist and Spider-Man saved him from the wreck.

techniques: Feather-blade wings that cut concrete and the plane's hull
Talons that grab, pin and slam
Chitauri gun (lost to Spider-Man on the ferry)

mechanisms: Metal plating that deflected FBI bullets
Absorbed a hit from a cargo plane turbine

weaknesses: Arc Reactor radiation short-circuited the Chitauri technology and overloaded the turbines, making the suit explode
mobility: High-speed flight on autonomous turbine wings
Matter phase shifters to pass through vehicles and hulls
limitations: All powers come from the exo-suit

sources.supports: Exo-suit: salvaged Chitauri tech, turbine wings, feather blades, talons, wing anchors, Chitauri gun, matter phase shifters, armor vs bullets and turbine, overload and explosion after the cargo plane crash, Spider-Man saving Toomes

notableResults.note: After the cargo plane crashed, the Arc Reactors' radiation overloaded his damaged suit, which exploded; Spider-Man pulled him from the remnants.

campaignTags.claim: Flies with the exo-suit's turbine wings.
Advanced exo-suit built from salvaged Chitauri technology.

unknowns: 'Catching fire' is not described on the opened page; it describes an overload and explosion.

feats.claim: Breached the Stark cargo plane in flight using a vacuum seal and matter phase shifters.
His suit's plating deflected FBI bullets and absorbed a hit from a cargo plane turbine.
